lead: Kansas City homes deal with flash floods, hail and frozen pipes. DryFlare helps owners from Brookside to the Northland get water out and dry fast.
risk: flash flooding along creeks, hail damage and frozen pipes
why: Brush Creek flooded the Country Club Plaza in September 1977, a disaster that led to years of flood work along the creek. Indian Creek, Blue River and Turkey Creek still flash flood in heavy storms. The Missouri River flooded parts of the area in 1993 and again in 2019.

Hail is common, and roofs across the metro take damage most springs. Over 60% of Kansas City homes were built before 1980, and many have basements, old clay sewer laterals and stone foundations. Winter cold snaps freeze pipes in outside walls.
image_alt: Aerial view of houses with torn roofs and fallen trees after a tornado
image_caption: Spring hail across Kansas City often leads to roof and ceiling leaks.
problems: Near Brush, Indian and Turkey creeks
Older homes in Midtown and Waldo
tips: Have the roof checked after hail.
Install a backwater valve if your basement has a floor drain.
Never drive through flooded streets near creeks.
areas: Calls come from the Crossroads, Westport, Brookside, Waldo, the Plaza, the Northland and River Market, plus Overland Park, Olathe, Independence, Lee's Summit and Kansas City, KS.

faq.q: Is hail damage common in Kansas City?
faq.a: Yes. The metro sees damaging hail most years. Cracked shingles let water into attics and ceilings, often weeks later. Inspect the roof after big storms and report damage quickly.
